Unofficial until approved by the

  MINUTES
  Regular Meeting
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  September 22, 2025
  6:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL: At 6:22 p.m., on Monday, September 22, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in the
Council Chambers of Alhambra City Hall.

PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Hembree, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks and Recreation Macias, Director
of Finance Lieu, Director of Community Development Ho, Director of Public Works and Utilities Ahlen,
Chief of Police Kennedy, Chief of Fire Department Ragusa, Director of Library Services LohGuan,
Director of Human Resources Ko, Management Analyst Alvarez, Public Information Specialist
Rodriguez

FLAG SALUTE:  Mayor Lee

LEE: Mayor Lee read the City’s Mission Statement as follows: The City of Alhambra is dedicated to
responsive, creative leadership and quality services, ensuring desirable neighborhoods and a
supportive business environment, while being sensitive to the diversity of our community.

LAND ACKNOWLEDGEMENT: We acknowledge that the land on which we are gathered is the
traditional, ancestral, and unceded territory of the Gabrielino/Tongva peoples. We seek to prioritize
respect for the historic culture and contemporary presence of the native peoples throughout California,
especially in the greater Los Angeles/Alhambra area. We come with respect and gratitude for the
Gabrielino/Tongva people who still consider themselves the caretakers of this land. It is through their
examples that we are reminded of our greater responsibility to take care of Mother Earth and to take
care of each other.

CEREMONIALS

1.  CERTIFICATE OF SERVICE: LORRAINE UWANAWICH – F2M25-3

  Mayor Lee and the City Council wished to commend and thank Executive Assistant to the City
  Manager Lorraine Uwanawich who was retiring after 36 years of faithful and loyal service to
  the Management Services Department and the City of Alhambra. Mayor Lee presented a
  Certificate of Service plaque to Ms. Uwanawich for her outstanding work for the City. Council
  offered kind words of gratitude and appreciation for Ms. Uwanawich and her work. Ms.
  UWANAWICH expressed her gratitude and appreciation for the City Council and staff
  throughout her career.

  their recent victory in the District 19 All Star Tournament. The team went on to place third in

PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-AGENDIZED ITEMS – F2M25-4

1) Nathan SONG, 222 N. Curtis Ave., expressed shock, as a member of the LGBTQ community, at
  the order of American flags being flown at half staff for the death of Charlie Kirk given his political
  2
9-22-25
   rhetoric. He questioned Council and staff in their choice to follow the federal policy and expressed
  concerns.

  City Manager BINNQUIST clarified that the City policy was to follow the federal notifications for
  flying the flag at half staff.

2) Cody CORBETT, 217 S. Granada Ave. spoke regarding demolition at 433 S. Hidalgo which he
  was concerned was done without a permit.

  Mayor LEE requested City Manager Binnquist email her about the address in question.

3) Illegal Immigrant expressed concerns regarding Council’s response to public speakers, the flag
  policy regarding other deaths in the community, criticized the City Manager and City Attorney,
  expressed concerns regarding treatment of the LGBT community, expressed concerns regarding
  the flag being lowered for Charlie Kirk’s death, supported reducing the public speaking time to 3
  minutes, and expressed concerns regarding ICE action in California.

4) Brian OTIS, 320 N. Monterey St., spoke regarding Council discussion of donating funds to the
  Alhambra Teacher’s Association Food Pantry. He discussed the City’s need to establish a policy
  regarding donations and made several suggestions.

5) Li’I FURUMOTO, 3030 W. Main St., representing Urban Visionaries and their partnership with the
  Alhambra Teachers Association for the Food Pantry. She expressed gratitude for the Council’s
  decision to support the Food Pantry, discussed the high need for the food program, and the
  expansion of the food program. She went on to discuss the response of the community to the
  organization and the organization’s decision to decline the contract with the City due to division in
  the community. She invited Council and the public who wished to volunteer to attend the next food
  distribution event and expressed best wishes for continued dialogue with the City.

  Mayor LEE discussed the numerous non-profits who continue to work within the community,
  expressed best wishes for Urban Visionaries and their continued work within the community,
  discussed the confusion, and discussed Staff’s work on a grant policy.

6) Charlie Kirk discussed attacks against the First Amendment, read excerpts from court cases,
  discussed issues of homelessness and vacant businesses, discussed housing issues, and spoke
  in support of President Trump’s immigration policies.

WANG: Councilmember WANG left Council Chambers at 7:15 p.m. and returned at 7:16 p.m.

7) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed SB79 and an update to the CalState LA
  Transit bus hub. He distributed handouts to Council, which are on file in the City Clerk’s office.

PRESENTATIONS

4.  SMOKE-FREE MULTI-UNIT HOUSING REGULATIONS – F2M25-7

  Management Analyst ALVAREZ delivered a staff report. On June 23, 2025, the City Council
  directed staff to research and provide information pertaining to ordinances prohibiting smoking
  in multi-unit residences. Staff presented information on this topic as it related to State law, the
  Alhambra Municipal Code, and smoke-free multi-unit ordinances from nine local municipalities
  as well as landlords’ discretion in the matter and implementation issues.

  Public Comment:

  The following people spoke in favor of Smoke-Free Multi-Unit Housing Regulations
  3
9-22-25
   1)  Antonio Salang, 11537 216th St., 90715, representing the Community Health Alliance
  2)  Jennifer Ng, S. Cordova St.
  3)  Esther Tam, 301 Orange Grove Ave.
  4)  Brian Otis, 320 N. Monterey St., also discussed the challenges of landlords to enforce
  smoking bans.
  5) Vincent Basobas, 112 N. 2nd St
  6) Je-Show Yang, 91803
  7) Yaneth Rodriguez
  8) Lewis McCammon, 105 N. Cordova St.
  9) Steven Gallegos, 500 N. Everett St.
  10) Shirley Tatsuno, 1408 S. Fifth St.
  11) Charlie Kirk
  12) Jonathan Grayson, via Zoom

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke in support of smoke-free
  regulations in Alhambra as well as her experiences as an asthma sufferer. She went on to
  speak regarding the graduated enforcement options as outlined in staff’s presentation. She
  stated that she did not support Police Officers enforcing regulations, but rather landlords and
  HOAs. Vice Mayor MALONEY spoke in support of regulations and echoed Ms. Andrade-
  Stadler’s comments regarding graduated enforcement and not directing Police or Code
  Enforcement Officers to enforce the regulations. Councilmember MAZA spoke in support of
  regulations and expressed concerns with the phase in period of enforcement. He also
  supported private enforcement. Mr. MAZA motioned to move forward with an ordinance. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER seconded the motion. Councilmember WANG spoke in support of the
  regulations. She discussed SB332 and suggested providing more educational efforts to inform
  the community about the dangers of second-hand smoke. She also cautioned that the
  regulations not push any families to eviction. Mayor LEE also spoke in support of regulations
  and echoed her colleagues’ comments. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, Mr. ALVAREZ, and Ms.
  BINNQUIST discussed other cities with graduated enforcement or “phased in” implementation.

  Mr. MAZA clarified his motion for an ordinance which would be a full ban on all indoor smoking
  in multi-unit housing complexes of four or more units, with a phase-in period of 2-3 years, that
  landlords immediately notify tenants of regulations, that education materials be provided, that
  tenants receive adequate noticing, that signage be required in units, and that the City work
  with other agencies. Ms. BINNQUIST and Mr. MAZA clarified a 3-year phase-in period.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the information regarding smoke-free
  multi-unit housing directed staff to draft an ordinance for Smoke-Free Multi-Unit Housing
  Regulations.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

5.  SURVEY REGARDING SET TIME LIMITS FOR PUBLIC COMMENT FOR NON-
  AGENDIZED ITEMS OR FOR CONSENT AGENDA ITEMS AND CONSIDERATION OF AN
  ORDINANCE AMENDING CHAPTER 2.04 OF THE ALHAMBRA MUNICIPAL CODE
  PERTAINING TO THE ORDER OF BUSINESS FOR CITY COUNCIL MEETINGS AND
  PROCEDURE FOR ADDRESSING COUNCIL – F2M24-7, O2M25-4850

  City Clerk MYLES delivered a staff report. At the September 8, 2025 Council meeting, staff
  presented a report summarizing how the placement of public comment for non-agendized
  items at the beginning of the meeting had functioned thus far, noting that the majority of
  individuals wishing to speak on a non-agendized item were able to do so during the initial 30-

  4
9-22-25
   minute comment period (with an average of six speakers) and that in those instances where
  there were speakers during the continuation of public comment at the end of the meeting, the
  average number of speakers was two. After receiving public comment, the City Council
  discussed a preference for keeping public comment for non-agendized items at the beginning
  of the meeting for an initial set time of 30 minutes with an individual speaker time of 3 minutes
  to allow for more individuals to make their comments at the beginning of the meeting. Council
  also discussed that an individual’s speaking time during the continuation of public comment at
  the end of the meeting could be 5 minutes, which could accommodate those that wished to
  have more time to speak. Council also directed staff to return with more information on whether
  surrounding cities have set time limits for public comment on non-agendized items and for
  consent agenda items. Staff reached out to surrounding cities in the area regarding set time
  limits for public comment for non-agendized items or for consent agenda items and a chart
  outlining staff’s survey results is attached the September 22, 2025 staff report by the City Clerk.
  Staff requested that the City Council determine which, if any, revisions to Chapter 2.04.030
  (Order of business for City Council meetings) and to Chapter 2.04.210 (Procedures for
  addressing Council) the Council wished to include in the proposed ordinance and then
  consider introducing the ordinance for first reading.

  Public Comment:

  1) Jennifer NG, S. Cordova St., spoke in support of the three-minute cap during the 30-minute
  period of Non-Agendized Public Comment at the beginning of the meeting. She did not
  support time limitations for the Consent Agenda comments. She asked for clarity regarding
  the effects of this decision on public comment at Board and Commission meetings.

  2) Kirk spoke regarding censorship issues, First Amendment issues, and limitations on
  democracy.

  3) Illegal Immigrant spoke against time limitations. He discussed public meetings of other
  agencies and requested information regarding School Board meetings. He further
  discussed suffering in the community and issues faced by undocumented residents and
  LGBT residents.

  4) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., supported the permanent 30-minute period for
  Non-Agenda Public Comment at the beginning of the meeting and supported a three-
  minute limit to allow for more speakers during that time. He did not support time limitations
  during the Consent Agenda or total speaking time of an individual speaker.

  5) Bert NG, via Zoom, supported the 30-minute period of Non-Agendized Public Comment at
  the start of the meeting but expressed concerns other time limitations on public speaking.
  He encouraged Council to take a stand against disruptive speakers at meetings.

  Discussion: Councilmember ANDRADE-STADLER spoke regarding the concerns of
  residents unable to fully access the public meetings and stated that there were several
  methods where the public were able to engage with the meeting including in person,
  telephone, email, and online. She supported 3 minutes speaking time per individual for the
  initial 30-minute period for Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning of the
  meeting and supported a 5-minute per individual speaking time for other items on the agenda.
  She discussed the time limitation for the Consent Agenda items and expressed some
  concerns. Vice Mayor MALONEY also supported 3 minutes speaking time for the 30-minute
  period for Non-Agendized Public Comment at the beginning of the meeting and 5-minute
  speaking time during the continuation of Public Comment on Non-Agendized Items at the end
  of the meeting. He did not support a per person total time limit during the meeting. He
  suggested that the person presiding over the meeting use discretion to impose limits when
  there are a large number of speakers. He stated that he was open to different ideas for
  speaking time during the Consent Agenda but remained undecided at the moment.

  5
9-22-25
   Councilmember MAZA also supported 3 minutes speaking time per individual for the 30-minute
  period for Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning of the meeting and
  supported continued review of the operation of meetings with input from the public. Regarding
  the Consent Agenda, he proposed that if an individual wished to speak on one item, then they
  be allowed five minutes of speaking time, but if an individual wished to speak on multiple items,
  then they have a maximum 10 minutes to speak on all items. He agreed that there should not
  be a total speaking time per meeting. Councilmember WANG supported 3 minutes speaking
  time for the initial 30-minute period for Public Comment on Non-Agendized items and a 5-
  minute speaking time per individual for Non-Agendized Public Comment at the end of the
  meeting. She did not agree with a total individual speaking time per meeting. She agreed with
  Mr. Maza’s suggestion for the Consent Agenda. Mayor LEE supported the initial 30-minute
  period for Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items at the beginning of the meeting and
  supported the Mayor’s discretion to limit speaking time if there are a large number of speakers
  present. She stated that she did not want to limit free speech or participation at public
  meetings. She did not support restrictions per person on their total speaking time. She was
  open to a set time of 3 minutes for the first 30 minutes, but expressed that she preferred this
  to be at the Mayor’s discretion depending on the number of speakers and felt that limitations
  were not necessary. She did not support the other limitations.

  Mr. MAZA motioned to permanently move Public Comment for Non-Agendized Items to the
  beginning of the meeting, after any ceremonial items, for an initial set time of 30 minutes with
  the balance of any comment at the end of the meeting, set the individual speaker time for
  public comment for non-agendized items to 3 minutes for the initial 30-minute comment period
  and to 5 minutes during the continuation of public comment at the end of the meeting, set the
  individual speaking time during the Consent Agenda to 5 minutes if speaking on one item and
  10 minutes total for those individuals speaking on 2 or more consent agenda items, and set
  speaking time to 5 minutes for regular agenda items. He also stated that this be attempted on
  a trial basis and be altered after that point. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER suggested that the trial
  basis be set at 6-months to review the practice. Mr. MAZA stated that he would like to make it
  permanent but requested a review after 6-months. Ms. ANDRADE-STADER seconded the
  motion. Ms. LEE and Mr. MAZA discussed his motion regarding enforcement of time
  limitations. City Attorney MONTES offered suggestions for public comment for Consent
  Agenda Items and stated that items which necessitated a broader discussion by the public
  could be pulled from the consent agenda and would therefore allow for 5 minutes speaking
  time for all individuals regarding that item.

  Action Taken:  City Council:

  1.  Received and filed the information report;
  2.  Determined the following revisions to be included in the proposed ordinance:

  a) Permanently move public comment for non-agendized items to the
  beginning of the meeting, after any ceremonial items, for an initial set time
  of 30 minutes with the balance of any comment at the end of the meeting.
  b) Set the individual speaker time for public comment for non-agendized
  items to 3 minutes for the initial 30-minute comment period and to 5
  minutes during the continuation of public comment at the end of the
  meeting.
  c) Set a total individual speaker time for consent agenda items to 5 minutes
  for one consent agenda item and 10 minutes for two or more consent
  agenda items.
  d) Set individual speaking time for all other agenda items to 5 minutes;

  3.  Requested a review all practices after a 6-month period;

  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Alhambra, California, amending

  Business for City Council meetings and Chapter 2.04.210 pertaining to the
  Procedure for Addressing Council

  which ordinance would return for a second reading and adoption at the next
  regular meeting.

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  ANDRADE-STADLER, MALONEY, MAZA, WANG

CONSENT AGENDA (Item Nos. 6 – 25)

All items listed under the Consent Agenda were considered by the City Council to be routine and were
enacted by one motion.

6.  HUD 2024-2025 CONSOLIDATED ANNUAL PERFORMANCE AND EVALUATION
  REPORT (CAPER) – F2M7-84, M2M25-135

  Each year, the City of Alhambra is required by the Department of Housing and Urban
  Development to prepare a Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER)
  for the CDBG and HOME programs. The CAPER summarizes program activities,
  expenditures, and accomplishments for the previous fiscal year and evaluates progress toward
  the goals and objectives outlined in the City’s One-Year Action Plan and Five-Year
  Consolidated Plan. The 2024-2025 program year represents the final year of the City’s 2020-
  2024 Five-Year Consolidated Plan. Over the five-year planning period, the City remained on
  track with its goals and successfully implemented a variety of programs to benefit low- and
  moderate- income residents. Staff requests that the City Council approve the 2024-2025
  Consolidated Annual Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) and direct staff to submit
  the report to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

  Public Comment:
  1) Illegal Immigrant requested clarification for assistance to illegal immigrant community,
  discussed the need for a homeless count, requested information regarding the homeless
  statistics for Alhambra and requested information regarding rent increases in Alhambra.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St. spoke regarding the CAPER and the HCDA Citizen
  Advisory Committee meetings. He also requested Council appoint new Committee members
  to fill the vacancies and help the Committee reach a quorum in order to review CDBG and
  HUD reports. He went on to speak regarding CDBG minor and major home rehabilitation
  programs.

WANG:  Councilmember Wang left Council Chambers at 9:16 p.m. and returned at 9:21 p.m.

  3) Kirk spoke regarding misuse of HUD funding for housing programs, homeless issues, and cited
  court cases. He went on to speak against illegal immigrants and spoke in support of President
  Trump.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the 2024-2025 Consolidated Annual
  Performance and Evaluation Report (CAPER) and directed staff to submit the report to HUD,
  as required. (M2M24-135)

7.  QUARTERLY CONTRACTS REPORT AS OF AUGUST 31, 2025 – F2M25-40

  On August 26, 2024, the City Council adopted Ordinance No. O2M24-4837, implementing the
  California Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act (CUPCCAA), as outlined in
  California Public Contract Code Sections 22000–22045. On April 14, 2025, the City Council
  adopted Ordinance No. O2M25-4845, updating contract thresholds in accordance with recent
  CUPCCAA amendments. During this meeting, the Council also requested a report identifying
  all contracts awarded between $50,000 and $75,000, which previously required Council
  approval before CUPCCAA implementation. During the reporting period of June 1, 2025
  through August 31, 2025, there were no contracts awarded in the amount of $50,000 to
  $75,000 without City Council approval.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council received and filed the quarterly contracts report for the
  period of June 1, 2025 through August 31, 2025.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

8.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION: FY 2023-24 SB1 STREET REHABILITATION PROJECT –
  F2M23-38, C2M25-18, M2M25-136

  On April 28, 2025, the City Council awarded a contract for the FY 2023-2024 SB1 Street
  Rehabilitation Project to Hardy & Harper, Inc. in the amount of $3,085,000.00. The project
  was completed in the amount of $2,906,579.49, due to a deletion of one area of paving,
  resulting in a reduction of $178,420.51 to the original contract. This project was inspected by
  staff and all work was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications.
  As such, it was appropriate for the City Council to accept this project as complete and instruct
  that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Hardy & Harper, Inc. for the FY
  2023-2024 SB1 Street Rehabilitation Project as complete in the amount of $2,906,579.49;
  directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of Completion with the County of Los Angeles for
  recordation; instructed the Finance Director to release the 5% retention 35 days from the date
  of recordation if no liens are filed; and, directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to
  finalize Council’s action. (M2M25-136)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

10.  AWARD CONTRACT: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES TO UPDATE THE
  SEWER MASTER PLAN – F2M25-44, RFP2M25-12, C2M25-40, M2M25-138

  On July 28, 2025, the City Council approved the distribution of a Request for Proposals for
  professional engineering services to Update the Sewer Master Plan. The Sewer Master Plan
  is intended to serve as a general, flexible, and open-ended document that requires periodic
  updates to consider changes in sewage generation, land development, infrastructure needs,
  and capital costs. The Sewer Master Plan evaluates the capacity and condition of the City’s
  sanitary sewer system and establishes the basis for the City’s ten-year sewer system Capital
  Improvement Program (CIP). Staff reviewed a total of two (2) proposals. ERSC was selected
  based on their distinguished qualifications, experience, reputation, responsiveness,
  availability, and cost.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a contract, subject to final language approval
  by the City Manager and City Attorney, by and between the City of Alhambra and Engineering
  Resources of Southern California (ERSC) for engineering services to update the Sewer Master
  Plan, in an amount not to exceed $239,450.00; and, directed staff to undertake the steps
  necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M25-138)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  LEE
  Ayes:  MALONEY, MAZA, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

 11.  DESIGNATION OF VOTING DELEGATE AND ALTERNATES FOR THE LEAGUE OF
  CALIFORNIA CITIES ANNUAL CONFERENCE – F2M25-13, M2M25-139

  The League of California Cities Annual Conference is scheduled for October 8th through 10th
  at the Long Beach Convention Center. During the Conference the League conducts its Annual
  Business Meeting during which the membership considers and takes action on resolutions
  that establish future League policy. In order for the City to have a vote at the Annual Business
  Meeting, it was necessary for the City Council to designate the voting delegate and alternates.
  Per the League’s Bylaws, only one Primary Delegate and two Alternates can be designated.
  It was anticipated that Vice Mayor Maloney and Councilmembers Maza and Wang would be
  present on Friday, October 10th when the Annual Business Meeting was scheduled; therefore,
  due to the fact that Mr. Maloney and Ms. Wang were already appointed as the City’s
  representatives for the League of California Cities, Los Angeles Board of Directors, staff
  proposed that Vice Mayor Maloney be appointed as the Voting Delegate for the City at the
  Annual Business Meeting and Councilmembers Wang and Maza be appointed as Voting
  Delegate Alternates.

  Public Comment:  Illegal Immigrant suggested topics for discussion at the League of
  California Cities Conference including speaking time during public meetings, suppression of
  public comment, homeless issues, and police issues.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the proposed appointment of Vice Mayor
  Maloney as Voting Delegate and Councilmembers Wang and Maza as Voting Delegate
  Alternates for the 2025 League of California Cities Conference’s Annual Business Meeting.

15.  AUTHORIZE RFP: PROFESSIONAL ENGINEERING SERVICES TO UPDATE THE WATER
  MASTER PLAN – F2M25-51, RFP2M25-21

  A Water Master Plan is a holistic and long-term strategic document that outlines the long-term
  vision and actions necessary to manage a community’s water resources. The City’s most
  recent Water Master Plan was prepared in 2004. Twenty years is a standard planning period
  for this type of study; far enough into the future that currently observable trends can be
  anticipated, and not so far into the future that the time frame exceeds our confidence. The
  purpose of the Water Master Plan is to provide the City with the road map to take us from the
  present to the future, confident that we have anticipated likely issues pertaining to our water
  service. A Water Master Plan includes a budget and financial program to fund the identified
  capital improvements. The plan offers a flexible, data-driven roadmap to guide the utility in
  prioritizing projects and adapting to changing circumstances. At its core, a Water Master Plan
  seeks to ensure the availability of clean water, protect the environment, and enhance the
  overall quality of life in the community.

  Discussion:  None.

25.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF AN ORDINANCE TO DESIGNATE FIRE HAZARD
  SEVERITY ZONES (FHSZ) WITHIN THE CITY OF ALHAMBRA PURSUANT TO
  CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 51178 AND THE CALIFORNIA FIRE CODE
  – F2M25-49, O2M25-4849

  Staff requested that the City Council declare introduced for second reading and adopt an
  Ordinance to designate Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the City of Alhambra (O2M25-
  4849). Pursuant to State law, the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection (CAL
  FIRE) - Office of the State Fire Marshal periodically updates Fire Hazard Severity Zone (FHSZ)
  maps for Local Responsibility Areas throughout the State. These maps identify varying levels
  of fire hazard (Moderate, High, and Very High) based on factors including vegetation,
  topography, weather, crown fire potential, fire history, and ember production and movement.
  State law requires local jurisdictions to designate FHSZ within their boundaries by ordinance
  to ensure proper implementation of associated building standards and fire safety requirements
  within identified zones. On March 24, 2025, CAL FIRE completed its latest assessment and
  released a map identifying FHSZ within the City of Alhambra. The City of Alhambra has not
  been included in the CAL FIRE FHSZ maps in the past. In the newly released maps,
  approximately less than one acre in Alhambra has been classified under the Very High
  Severity Zone designation. There are two parcels affected on Sherwood Avenue and two
  parcels on Keats Street. The City posted the map and information regarding FHSZ on the
  City’s website at https://www.alhambraca.gov/863/FireHazard-Severity-Zones. The City
  Council gave first reading to this ordinance at the September 8, 2025 Council meeting.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council declared introduced for its second reading and adopt the
  following ordinance entitled:

  Ordinance No. O2M25-4849: An Ordinance of the Alhambra City
  Council to designate Fire Hazard Severity Zone
